editorial_corrections: OLS residuals are orthogonal to fitted regressors in-sample with an intercept, not necessarily statistically independent.
Strong negative correlation also contributes to collinearity; pairwise correlation is not a complete matrix-rank test.
Ridge uses squared L2; scikit-learn Ridge and Lasso/Elastic Net use different loss normalizations.
L1 is not the count of nonzero coefficients; best-subset constraints are combinatorial.
The lecture and lab illustrate different fold counts; the original examples use chronological expanding windows with fold-local scaling and a separate final test.
James-Stein Normal-means improvements require specified distribution, dimension and loss assumptions and do not guarantee each component or regression prediction improves.
Contemporaneous factor regressions and ex-post partitions by realized target sign do not establish an ex-ante trading forecast.
Monthly expectation multiplied by twelve is arithmetic annualization, not CAGR.
A factor proxy is not automatically a causal economic quantity.

original_examples.validation: 120 synthetic months, development first 96, final test last 24; expanding training windows 60, 72 and 84 with 12-month validation blocks
